# Design systems

kala ships 12 complete design systems, each authored as a whole: the fonts, spacing, colour
strategy, corner radius, and motion were chosen together, the way a designer would choose
them.

When you ask kala to set up a design system, it reads your brief, scores all 12, and offers
you the best three. You pick one. See [Your first project](02-first-project.md) for that
flow.

---

## The 12 systems

| `sunlit-wellness` | wellness, meditation, mindful, +4 more | Outfit / Fraunces | 17px | 1.333 | 4px generous | 20px | shadows | moderate, 240ms |
| `technical-mono` | developer, devtool, cli, +4 more | IBM Plex Sans / IBM Plex Serif | 14px | 1.2 | 4px tight | 2px | borders | minimal, 100ms |
| `warm-utility` | small business, invoicing, booking, +3 more | Public Sans / Source Serif 4 | 16px | 1.25 | 4px normal | 8px | borders | moderate, 180ms |
<!-- kala:docs:systems:end -->

**Reading the table:** `Base` is the body text size in px and `Ratio` the multiplier between
type steps. `Space` is the spacing unit every padding and gap is a multiple of. `Depth` is
whether the system separates things with borders or with shadows.

---

## What each system refuses to do

Every system carries **signature rules** — the specific opinions that stop output reading
generic — and **anti-defaults**, patterns it will not use. kala injects these into every
brief and guide response, so they become constraints your agent works under.

<!-- kala:docs:signatures:start — generated by scripts/build-docs.mjs, do not edit -->
| System | Signature rules | Will not use |
|---|---|---|
| `archive-serif` | • Body copy is serif and set at a comfortable reading size. • Citations and metadata sit in the sans, one step down. • Navigation is a table of contents, not a toolbar. • Dates are written in full, never relative. | `infinite-scroll`, `card-grid-everything`, `drop-shadows` |
| `bold-commerce` | • The accent colour belongs to the buy button and nothing else. • Product imagery is never cropped into a circle. • Price is the second-largest thing on the card, after the image. • Scarcity claims must be true or absent. | `fake-countdown`, `carousel-hero`, `gray-on-color` |
| `dense-console` | • Every row is scannable at a glance; nothing animates on data change. • Colour means severity and nothing else. • Numbers are tabular so columns align to the digit. • Density is the feature — do not add padding to make it breathe. | `card-in-card`, `hover-reveal-actions`, `animated-counters` |
| `editorial-clean` | • Type leads. Measure is capped near 68 characters. • Headings use the serif; interface chrome uses the sans. • Rules are hairlines, and there are very few of them. • Images run full-measure or full-bleed, never in cards. | `card-grid-everything`, `rounded-corners`, `drop-shadows` |
| `muted-enterprise` | • Every destructive action needs a typed confirmation. • Labels sit above fields, never inside them as placeholders. • Permissions and ownership are always visible, never inferred. • Nothing is hidden behind hover; keyboard reaches everything. | `placeholder-as-label`, `hover-only-actions`, `gradient-anything` |
| `playful-rounded` | • Touch targets are never smaller than 48px. • Success is celebrated; failure is never punished visually. • Icons always pair with a word, because readers are learning. • Motion overshoots slightly on reward, never on navigation. | `dense-data-grid`, `all-caps-labels`, `tiny-tap-targets` |
| `quiet-precision` | • Borders carry structure. Shadows are for overlays only. • Numbers are tabular-lined and right-aligned. • One accent, used only for the single primary action per surface. • Section breaks are space, never rules. | `card-in-card`, `gradient-anything`, `shadow-on-rest-state` |
| `soft-clinical` | • Never use red for anything except genuine danger. • Every number carries its unit, spelled out. • Forms ask one question per screen where the stakes are high. • Reassurance sits next to the action, not in a tooltip. | `urgency-banners`, `countdown-timers`, `dark-patterns` |
| `stark-brutal` | • Type is enormous or it is small; nothing sits in between. • Borders are 2px and black. There are no shadows anywhere. • Layout is asymmetric on purpose and holds its grid. • Hover states invert rather than fade. | `drop-shadows`, `rounded-corners`, `gradient-anything` |
| `sunlit-wellness` | • One action per screen; nothing competes for attention. • Streaks are encouraged, never enforced with guilt. • Generous negative space is the point, not wasted room. • Transitions are slow enough to feel like breathing. | `urgency-banners`, `dense-data-grid`, `red-error-states` |
| `technical-mono` | • Monospace for every identifier, path, and value — never for prose. • Status is a colored dot plus a word, never colour alone. • Dense by default; whitespace is earned, not assumed. • Destructive actions are outlined, never filled. | `gradient-anything`, `rounded-pill-buttons`, `illustration-empty-states` |
| `warm-utility` | • Rounded corners and warm neutrals; nothing clinical. • Empty states speak in plain sentences, never in icons alone. • Primary action is a filled button; everything else is text or outline. • Errors are amber before they are red. | `pure-gray-neutrals`, `all-caps-labels`, `dense-data-grid` |
<!-- kala:docs:signatures:end -->

---

## The catalog fallback tier

If your brief does not fit any of the 12 well (a fit score below 0.55), kala falls through
to a much larger, less opinionated pool: 84 styles, 192 palettes, and 74 font pairings,
selected independently and combined. See [Catalog](05-catalog.md).

A proposal from the fallback tier has **no signature rules and no anti-defaults** — that is
the trade. It still gets a fully contrast-solved palette; nothing skips the colour solver.
